title: The Addams Family
description: Fictional family created by Charles Addams
wiki_lead:
The Addams Family is a fictional family and franchise created by American cartoonist Charles Addams. The Addams are an eccentric old-money clan who delight in the macabre and the grotesque and are seemingly unaware or unconcerned that other people find them bizarre or frightening. The family's view in seeing their family life and interests as normal was a basis for the satire and comedy.  They originally appeared in a series of 150 standalone single-panel comics, about half of which were originally published in The New Yorker between 1938 and their creator's death in 1988. They have since appeared in other media, such as television, film, video games, comic books, a musical, and merchandise.
The family members were unnamed until the 1960s. Matriarch Morticia and daughter Wednesday received their names when a licensed doll collection was released in 1962; patriarch Gomez and son Pugsley were named when the 1964 television series debuted. The Addams Family consists of Gomez and Morticia Addams, their children, Wednesday and Pugsley, and close family members Uncle Fester and Grandmama, their butler Lurch, and Pugsley's pet octopus, Aristotle. The dimly seen Thing (later a disembodied hand) was introduced in 1954, and Gomez's Cousin Itt, Morticia's pet lion Kitty Kat and Morticia's carnivorous plant Cleopatra in 1964. Pubert Addams, Wednesday and Pugsley's infant brother, was introduced in the 1993 film Addams Family Values.
The live-action television series premiered on ABC on Friday, September 18, 1964, and ran for two seasons. An animated series from Hanna-Barbera aired in 1973 and the characters had cameos in the animated The New Scooby-Doo Movies.  The 1960s television show characters and actors returned in a 1977 telefilm titled Halloween with the New Addams Family. 
The franchise was revived in the 1990s with a feature film series consisting of The Addams Family (1991) and Addams Family Values (1993). The films inspired a second animated series (1992–1993) which is set in the same fictional universe. The series was rebooted with a 1998 direct-to-video film and a spin-off live-action television series (1998–1999). In 2010, a live musical adaptation featuring Nathan Lane and Bebe Neuwirth opened on Broadway to tepid reviews, but it was nominated for two Tony Awards and eight Drama Desk Awards, winning one Drama Desk Award for Outstanding Set Design. The series was rebooted again in 2019 with the animated film The Addams Family, which led to a sequel in 2021. In 2022, Netflix debuted the original live action series Wednesday, based around the daughter of the family.
The franchise has spawned a video game series, academic books and soundtracks, which are based around its Grammy-nominated theme song. A staple in pop culture for eight decades, The Addams Family has influenced American comics, cinema and television. The goth subculture and its fashion have also been influenced by The Addams Family.

grok_lead: The Addams Family is a fictional American family of eccentrically macabre characters created by cartoonist Charles Addams, who first depicted them as unnamed ghoulish figures in a single-panel gag cartoon published in The New Yorker on August 6, 1938. The family resides in a dilapidated Gothic mansion and embodies dark humor through their fascination with the morbid, supernatural, and unconventional, contrasting sharply with mainstream societal norms. Core members include the passionate patriarch Gomez Addams, the elegant and poised matriarch Morticia Addams, their inventive children Wednesday and Pugsley, the bald and explosive Uncle Fester, the hulking butler Lurch, the disembodied hand Thing, the diminutive and incomprehensible Cousin Itt, and the potion-brewing Grandmama. Addams produced 58 such cartoons featuring the family out of over 1,300 total works for the magazine between 1935 and 1988, often without captions to let the visuals convey the twisted wit. The family's transition from print to other media began with the naming of characters for merchandise, such as 1962 Ideal Toys dolls that assigned names like Gomez and Morticia, which were later canonized in adaptations. The first major adaptation was the ABC sitcom The Addams Family, which aired from September 18, 1964, to April 8, 1966, spanning 64 black-and-white episodes and starring John Astin as Gomez and Carolyn Jones as Morticia. Produced by Filmways with David Levy as executive producer, the series expanded the characters' backstories and household dynamics, introducing elements like the family's pet lion Kitty and a home UNIVAC computer, while emphasizing their loving, supportive relationships amid the grotesquerie. It competed directly with the similarly themed The Munsters but distinguished itself by focusing on sophisticated eccentricity rather than outright monstrosity, gaining a cult following through syndication despite modest initial ratings. Subsequent adaptations revitalized the franchise across film, animation, and theater. The 1991 Paramount film directed by Barry Sonnenfeld, starring RaÃºl JuliÃ¡ as Gomez and Anjelica Huston as Morticia, grossed $191 million worldwide and spawned a 1993 sequel, Addams Family Values, which highlighted Christina Ricci's portrayal of a sardonic Wednesday and earned $48.9 million. Animated iterations include Hanna-Barbera's short-lived 1973 series and a 1992-1993 version, followed by MGM's 2019 and 2021 feature films voicing the family with talents like Oscar Isaac and Charlize Theron. A 2010 Broadway musical ran for nearly two years, becoming a global touring production and inspiring high school performances as the most licensed musical in North America for the 2018-2019 school year. In recent years, the Addams Family has seen renewed popularity through streaming, particularly Netflix's Wednesday (2022âpresent), a Tim Burton-directed series centered on Jenna Ortega's teenage Wednesday Addams at Nevermore Academy, which became one of the platform's most-watched English-language shows in its first season. Season 2, now streaming as of September 2025, expands the family dynamics with returning cast members including Luis GuzmÃ¡n as Gomez, Catherine Zeta-Jones as Morticia, and Fred Armisen as Uncle Fester, alongside guest appearances like Christopher Lloyd reprising his 1990s film role. A new animated film reboot is in development by Wednesday creators Alfred Gough and Miles Millar, announced in 2025, further extending the franchise's legacy. Throughout its nearly 90-year history, The Addams Family has endured as a cultural icon, celebrating outsider perspectives and familial bonds through its blend of horror and comedy, influencing merchandise, Halloween traditions, and modern gothic aesthetics.
